S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.

subtypes.Interference by Worry: Unable to focus on the task at hand because worries keep surfacing.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Attention is scattered due to anxiety, making it hard to focus on one thing for long.
subtypes.Mind Going Blank: Suddenly the mind goes empty or white, and no thoughts occur.

patient_info.stressor: Denise enrolled in an evening graduate certificate program in analytics while continuing her demanding Manhattan management analyst role, expecting that her usual calendars and spreadsheets would make the added workload manageable. Across the following 1 year and 3 months, worries about tuition, work performance, grades, future competitiveness, family expectations, and everyday obligations became persistent and difficult to control, with worsening sleep, exhaustion, and trouble concentrating on financial models and class assignments. The impairment became clinically significant when she began missing deadlines, rereading routine material repeatedly without retaining it, and withdrawing from yoga, running, and cooking because she felt consumed by planning and second-guessing. After a strained performance meeting at work and a separate warning from an instructor about incomplete coursework, she contacted her employer’s assistance program and was referred for psychiatric evaluation.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I’m here because my sleep has basically fallen apart—I’ll lie in bed in my apartment for hours with my laptop closed, still mentally rechecking work deadlines, tuition payments, and class assignments, and even when I do sleep I wake up feeling like I never really turned off.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: By midafternoon at the office I feel completely drained, like even answering emails or walking to the subway takes effort, and resting on the weekend doesn’t seem to give me my energy back.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.
S056.manifestation: My mind keeps jumping from whether I’m falling behind at work, to whether I’m wasting money on school, to whether my family will think I can’t handle things, and I treat every small issue like it could derail my whole future.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.
S057.manifestation: I try to tell myself to stop and focus on one thing, but one worry immediately leads to another until I’m checking my calendar, my budget, and my assignments over and over instead of actually getting anything done.

S059.name: Concentration_Difficulty
S059.description: Difficulty concentrating or mind going blank.
S059.manifestation: I’ll stare at the same financial model or class reading for ages and realize I’ve reread the same paragraph five times without absorbing it, because my head is already off running through everything that could go wrong.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve started missing work deadlines and falling behind in my certificate classes, and I’ve stopped doing the routines that used to keep me grounded, like yoga, running, and cooking.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and three months, since I started the evening graduate certificate program while keeping my full-time analyst job.
